You are matching code-review findings against a known bug. Reply with ONLY a JSON object.

KNOWN BUG: Clearing the combobox never calls onChange(null), so the selection can't be cleared.

Rules:
- Answer "yes" only if the text describes THIS specific bug: the same faulty behaviour in the same situation. A finding about a nearby but different behaviour (another header, another edge case, a different race) is "no".
- A finding that says the behaviour was checked and PASSED, or that the code handles it correctly, is "no".
- Wording does not matter; the behaviour does.
- For handoffs: count only text that tells the implementor to fix this bug (a reported finding, a fix instruction). Restated acceptance criteria that merely describe the desired behaviour do NOT count as carrying the finding unless the handoff ties them to a reported failure.

=== REVIEW 1 FINDINGS ===
- [blocking] Tabs fallback ignores DOM order (T5, README line 33). `Tabs` uses `enabled[0]` from `entries`, which is registration order. Repro: mount `<Tabs defaultValue="zzz">` with tabs b, c, then rerender with `<Tab value="a">` before them. `expect(selected.map(t=>t.textContent)).toEqual(["A"])` got `['B']`. Reorder `[a,b]` to `[b,a]` gives `aria-selected` false on the first tab. The `tabIndex=0` stop lands on the wrong tab.
- [blocking] Backdrop drag closes the dialog (D4, README line 86 "press and release on the backdrop"). Pressing on the backdrop and releasing inside the content fires `click` on the backdrop (common ancestor), and `pressedOnBackdrop` is true, so `onOpenChange(false)` runs. Repro with `user.pointer([{keys:"[MouseLeft>]",target:backdrop},{target:text},{keys:"[/MouseLeft]",target:text}])`: spy called once, expected zero. The mirror case in the criterion is tested, but this direction is not.
- [blocking] Escape ignored when focus is on body (D4 "Escape calls onOpenChange(false)"). Repro: the dialog's focused button calls `setShow(false)`, so `document.activeElement` is body. `user.keyboard("{Escape}")` leaves `onOpenChange` uncalled. The fix is a document-level Escape listener or a focus fallback. Focus-dependent, so this is judgement, but the criterion is unqualified.
- [minor] A Tab with no matching TabPanel has a dangling `aria-controls` (reproduced: `aria-controls «r0»-panel-a` resolves to null).
- [minor] Uncontrolled Tabs: a selected tab that is removed and later re-added is selected again, because internal state was never cleared (not reproduced as a criterion failure).
- [minor] Combobox with duplicate option values gives two `aria-selected="true"` options (reproduced).
- [minor] Dialog stale press flag: mousedown on backdrop, release elsewhere, then a bare click on the backdrop closes the dialog. Only reproduced with synthetic events that have no matching mousedown; not reproduced in a realistic sequence.
- [minor] Two Dialogs mounted open together: the outer dialog's focus effect runs last and steals focus from the inner one (reproduced; Escape then closes the outer dialog).
=== REVIEW 2 FINDINGS ===
- [blocking] Dialog stale press flags: a right-button press and release on the backdrop leaves `pressedOnBackdrop` and `releasedOnBackdrop` both true with no click to reset them. A later click on content, such as keyboard Enter on the "Ok" button, then closes the dialog. Reproduced: `fireEvent.mouseDown(backdrop,{button:2})`, `mouseUp(backdrop,{button:2})`, focus the button, `user.keyboard("{Enter}")` gives `onOpenChange` called with `false`. Fix idea: reset both refs on every mousedown, or check `event.button === 0`.
- [blocking] Dialog Escape order for nested dialogs mounted open together: effects run child-first, so the inner dialog is pushed onto `openDialogs` before the outer one and the outer is treated as topmost. Reproduced: `<Dialog open title="Outer"><Dialog open title="Inner">` with one Escape gives outer calls 1, inner calls 0. The later-opened case (inner opened by a click) passes. Fix idea: push in render or in a layout effect, or order the stack by DOM position.
- [blocking] Tabs checklist ("every referenced id exists"): a Tab with no matching TabPanel has `aria-controls` pointing at a missing id. Reproduced: `document.getElementById(aria-controls)` is null for a lone `<Tab value="a">`. Fix idea: omit `aria-controls` when no panel exists, or document the requirement.
- [minor] Tabs controlled with a value that matches no tab: the first tab is visibly selected, but clicking it does not call `onValueChange`, so the parent never learns the displayed selection. Not clearly against the spec's "only when the selection changes", so I am not calling it a bug.
- [minor] Tabs with every tab disabled: all tabs get tabIndex -1, so the tablist cannot be reached by keyboard. Consistent with the spec, but worth a note.
- [minor] Tabs removing the selected tab and re-adding it: the tab is selected again because internal state still holds its value. Not reproduced as a bug.
- [minor] Combobox `onChange` is called with the same value when the user re-selects the current option. The spec does not mention this. Not reproduced as a bug.

GOAL: Fix the reviewer and maintainer findings below in the existing accessible React 19 component library (Tabs, Dialog, Combobox). Add a failing test for each finding first, then fix it. Finish with `pnpm test` and `pnpm typecheck` passing.

FILES: Repo /tmp/ff-eval-tfj8v1pl/workspace. Source: src/Tabs.tsx, src/Dialog.tsx, src/Combobox.tsx. Tests: tests/Tabs.test.tsx, tests/Dialog.test.tsx, tests/Combobox.test.tsx. Docs: README.md. Conventions: FEATURE_FLOW.md.
- Tabs keeps a registry (`entries`). Each Tab registers itself in useLayoutEffect, and `selected` falls back to the first enabled entry. Keyboard handling uses live DOM order through querySelectorAll in TabList.
- Dialog renders a backdrop div with onMouseDown/onClick handlers and a `pressedOnBackdrop` ref. Inside it is a role=dialog div whose onKeyDown handles Tab (`trapTab`) and Escape (ignored when defaultPrevented). A useEffect on `[open]` moves focus in and restores it.
- Combobox state is `internal`, `open`, `query` (null means "show the selected label") and `active`. On Escape while open, it calls preventDefault and stopPropagation.

CONSTRAINTS: No new dependencies. Don't edit package.json, tsconfig, vitest config, the lockfile or FEATURE_FLOW.md. Keep public prop names unchanged. Keep every existing test passing; only change a test where its expectation is the bug being fixed.

FINDINGS TO FIX:
1. [blocking, T5] The Tabs fallback uses registration order instead of DOM order. Repro: `<Tabs defaultValue="zzz">` with tabs b and c, then rerender with `<Tab value="a">` inserted before them. B ends up selected; A should be. Compute the fallback from DOM order, for example by storing the button element in each entry and sorting with compareDocumentPosition. Reordering [a,b] to [b,a] with a non-matching defaultValue should select the first tab in the DOM.
2. [blocking, D4] Pressing on the backdrop and releasing inside the dialog content closes the dialog, because the click fires on the common ancestor (the backdrop). Close only when the press started on the backdrop and the release was on the backdrop too. Track both mousedown and mouseup targets, and reset the flags after each click. The repro must not call onOpenChange: `user.pointer([{keys:"[MouseLeft>]",target:backdrop},{target:textInside},{keys:"[/MouseLeft]",target:textInside}])`. The existing reverse case (press inside, release on the backdrop) must still not close, and a plain click on the backdrop must still close.
3. [blocking, D4] Escape does nothing when focus has dropped to document.body while the dialog is open, for example after the focused button inside was removed. Handle Escape with a document-level keydown listener registered while the dialog is open. Keep a module-level stack of open dialogs so only the topmost one closes, and ignore events that are already defaultPrevented. An open Combobox inside a Dialog must still close only its popup on Escape. It calls stopPropagation and preventDefault; check that this still works with the document listener. Nested dialogs must close only the top one.
4. [blocking] Focus trap: React events bubble through portals, so an outer dialog's Tab handler also runs for Tab presses inside a nested inner dialog. If the outer dialog has no focusable children, it pulls focus to itself. Fix: skip trapping when the event is already defaultPrevented, or when it came from inside a different (nested) dialog. Test it with a nested dialog whose outer dialog has no focusable children: Tab inside the inner dialog keeps focus in the inner dialog.
5. [blocking] Combobox can't clear the selection back to null. If the user empties the input text (query === "") and then presses Enter with no active option, or blurs the input, and there is a current value, call onChange(null). In uncontrolled mode also set the internal value to null. Don't call it when the value is already null. Note: after typing "" the active option resets to the first enabled match. Decide how Enter behaves then, and pick the simplest rule that lets keyboard users clear. Suggestion: an empty query plus Enter clears only when no option is active; an empty query plus blur always clears. Document the rule in README. Test both Enter and blur.
6. [minor] Tabs: before any tab registers (first render, SSR), `selected` is undefined, so no tab is tabbable and every panel is hidden. When `entries` is empty, use the requested value (value, or else the internal defaultValue) as selected.
7. [minor] Update the README backdrop sentence to match: the dialog closes only when the press and the release are both on the backdrop. Document the clear-to-null behavior from item 5.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
General
- G1. `src/index.ts` exports Tabs, TabList, Tab, TabPanel, Dialog, Combobox and their props types (TabsProps, TabListProps, TabProps, TabPanelProps, DialogProps, ComboboxProps, ComboboxOption). `pnpm test` and `pnpm typecheck` pass.
- G2. Style-agnostic: no styles shipped; each component accepts `className` and passes extra native HTML attributes through to its main element (Tab -> button, TabList/TabPanel -> div, Dialog -> the role=dialog element, Combobox -> the input), while the component's own ARIA attributes and handlers still apply (user onKeyDown/onClick are called, not replaced).
- G3. README.md documents every component: a props table (name, type, required/default, description) and a keyboard table, plus a short usage example; every claim in it is backed by code and a test.

Tabs
- T1. `<Tabs>` works uncontrolled (`defaultValue`) and controlled (`value` + `onValueChange`). With no defaultValue/value, the first non-disabled tab is selected. In controlled mode, a parent that ignores onValueChange keeps the old tab selected. onValueChange fires with the new value only when the selection actually changes (not when re-selecting the current tab).
- T2. Roles/ARIA: TabList is role="tablist" with the given aria-label (and aria-orientation="horizontal" is fine); each Tab is a `<button type="button" role="tab">` with aria-selected true/false, aria-controls = its panel's id, and id referenced by its panel's aria-labelledby; disabled tabs have aria-disabled="true" or disabled and cannot be selected by click or keyboard. TabPanel is role="tabpanel", tabIndex=0, aria-labelledby its tab; only the selected panel is shown (others are not rendered or have `hidden`). Ids must be valid even when tab values contain spaces or special characters (e.g. value "a b" or "x/y") — derive ids from useId plus an index or sanitized value, and ids must be unique across two Tabs instances on one page using the same values.
- T3. Only the selected tab has tabIndex=0; all other tabs have tabIndex=-1. Tab key from outside lands on the selected tab; Tab from the selected tab moves to the panel.
- T4. ArrowRight/ArrowLeft move focus to the next/previous enabled tab, wrapping at the ends and skipping disabled tabs; Home/End move to the first/last enabled tab. Selection follows focus (the focused tab becomes selected, onValueChange called). Other keys do nothing and arrow keys call preventDefault.
- T5. Hostile: all tabs disabled except one (arrows keep focus on it, no crash); first and last tabs disabled (Home/End land on the first/last ENABLED tab, wrapping skips them); defaultValue that matches no tab (falls back to first enabled tab, or at least no crash and some tab is focusable); tabs added/removed after mount (keyboard order follows DOM order of the current tabs).

Dialog
- D1. `<Dialog open onOpenChange title description? >children</Dialog>`: when open is false nothing is rendered; when true it renders via createPortal into document.body a backdrop element and an element with role="dialog", aria-modal="true", aria-labelledby pointing to a rendered heading containing `title`, and aria-describedby pointing to an element containing `description` only when description is given (no aria-describedby attribute otherwise). Also accept `className` for the dialog element.
- D2. On open, focus moves inside the dialog: to the first focusable element in it, or to the dialog element itself (tabIndex=-1) if it has none.
- D3. Focus trap: Tab from the last focusable wraps to the first, Shift+Tab from the first wraps to the last; with no focusable children, Tab keeps focus on the dialog. Focusable query must skip disabled elements, tabindex="-1", and hidden inputs.
- D4. Escape calls onOpenChange(false). A mousedown+click on the backdrop (outside the dialog content) calls onOpenChange(false); a click inside the dialog content does NOT. A click that starts inside the content and ends on the backdrop (e.g. drag-select) should not close — track pointerdown/mousedown target.
- D5. When the dialog closes (open goes false, or it unmounts), focus returns to the element that was focused before it opened, if it is still in the document.
- D6. Hostile: Escape inside a Combobox inside the Dialog — if the combobox popup is open, its Escape handling should stop propagation so only the popup closes (Combobox calls stopPropagation/preventDefault on Escape when it was open; Dialog ignores already-defaultPrevented Escape events). Opening with `open` initially true at mount also moves focus in and later restores. onOpenChange not called when the parent keeps open=true (controlled) — dialog just stays open.

Combobox
- C1. `<Combobox label options value onChange placeholder?>`; options: `{ value: string; label: string; disabled?: boolean }`; value is `string | null`; onChange(value: string | null). Controlled by `value`. Also support uncontrolled: if `value` prop is undefined, use `defaultValue?: string | null` internal state. Document this in README.
- C2. Markup: a visible `<label>` associated with an `<input role="combobox">` (getByRole('combobox', {name: label}) works), aria-autocomplete="list", aria-expanded true/false, aria-controls = the listbox id; popup is `role="listbox"` (with aria-label or aria-labelledby the label); options are role="option" with unique valid ids, aria-selected true for the selected value, aria-disabled="true" for disabled ones. placeholder is passed to the input.
- C3. The input shows the selected option's label when closed. Typing opens the listbox and filters options whose label contains the typed text case-insensitively (e.g. "AP" matches "Apple" and "Grape"). Clearing the text shows all options.
- C4. ArrowDown opens the popup if closed; when open, ArrowDown/ArrowUp move the active option (aria-activedescendant on the input = active option id, active option gets a data-active or similar marker attr is optional), skipping disabled options, wrapping at ends (document whichever: wrap). DOM focus stays on the input. When the list is filtered, the active option resets to the first enabled match (or none).
- C5. Enter on an active option calls onChange(option.value), closes the popup, and sets the input text to that label. Enter with no active option does nothing (and doesn't submit a surrounding form if popup is open — preventDefault when open). Clicking an enabled option selects it the same way (use onMouseDown preventDefault so input keeps focus); clicking a disabled option does nothing.
- C6. Escape closes the popup without calling onChange and restores the input text to the selected option's label (or empty if none); aria-expanded becomes false and aria-activedescendant is removed.
- C7. When nothing matches, the popup shows a "No results" message (e.g. a `<div role="status">` or an option-less listbox sibling with text "No results"); no role="option" elements rendered; Enter does nothing.
- C8. Blur (focus leaving the input) closes the popup and restores the text to the selected label.
- C9. Hostile: all options disabled (ArrowDown sets no active option, no infinite loop); empty options array (shows "No results" when opened); option values with spaces/special chars produce valid unique ids; typed text with regex characters like "(" or "." or "[" must not throw (use string includes, not RegExp); a value prop that matches no option shows empty input; the controlled value changing externally updates the displayed text; label text with different case/whitespace still matches by includes on lowercase.

(Items 5 and 6 above refine C5, C8 and T1. Where they conflict with the older wording, the findings win: emptying the text and blurring clears to null.)
